ledger.claim: The excess is established on this trip's own measurement. The trace length is 22.5 km against a booked optimal of 18.0 km, an excess of 4.5 km and 25.00% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass: the excess exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms and exceeds 20% of optimal. Under POL-RD-01 the governing field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, and here the rounded trip_record copy (22.5 km) agrees with it, so the threshold is met on either figure.

The trace is clean, and POL-RD-07 cannot be used to dilute it. It carries 177 fixes at a 10 second sample interval against a 10 second expected interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0. None of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) fires, so the deviation may stand on the gps_trace alone, no independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) is required, and the mandatory escalation in POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The admissibility pre-pass agrees: EV-GPS-02808 is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0.

The driver's traffic advisory does not exonerate him, because POL-RD-03 requires all three of its limbs. Limb (c) demands an actual route that leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after. The record's own geometry check on the trace shows the vehicle's closest approach to the advisory area is 1,203.39 m, with 0 fixes inside that area and trace_enters_area false. A route that never comes within 1.2 km of the affected area did not route around it, so limb (c) fails and POL-RD-03 is unavailable. The advisory artifact's own note records that this check is the closest available test of limb (c) on this record.

Limb (a) of POL-RD-03 is likewise not made out on the record, and the burden is the driver's. The advisory names the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos Link, but the optimal route's polyline is not in the record, so nothing establishes that the optimal route traverses the affected segment as limb (a) requires. The rider has already discharged his side under POL-RD-08: the trip identifiers and pickup timing match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and the threshold excess is shown on an unimpaired trace. The driver must then point to a specific artifact and a specific clause that excuses the excess; an untested assertion of 'accident on the PIE' does not discharge that burden. The advisory's window (06:09:18 to 07:33:38) does overlap the trip (06:39:18 to 07:08:38) so limb (b) is met, but all three limbs are conjunctive and two of them are not.

Even taken at its highest, the advisory's own figures do not fit the drive. The advisory records the shortest lawful alternative over the booked endpoints as 21.0 km, yet the driver's trace runs 22.5 km - 1.5 km longer than the alternative the driver says he took, and 4.5 km longer than the booked optimal. That comparison is arithmetic on the record and is at least consistent with the vehicle not having followed the alternative the advisory documents, which is further reason to find limb (c) unsatisfied.

Nothing in the chat_log shifts any part of the excess to the rider. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log that identifies an actionable place or road and is corroborated by the trace. The trip carries exactly one message, sent by the DRIVER at 06:40:48 - 'accident on the PIE ahead, taking the alternative' - with waypoint_hint null. There is no rider instruction at all, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable, no distance is excluded, and the driver's own route choice cannot be billed to the rider as if the rider had asked for it.

The baseline has not moved. POL-RD-05 requires an amended pickup or dropoff with a stored amended optimal. On this trip pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so no re-quote exists, the clause cannot be run, and the comparison point remains the booked optimal of 18.0 km.

No part of the 4.5 km excess is attributable to a co-rider. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12 does not apply and the matched-itinerary baseline it substitutes for is not in play. The baseline is trip_record.optimal_distance_km of 18.0 km.

The distance-and-time refund route is open, because the fare model is metered. The fare breakdown records fare_model METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 (upfront-quoted fares) does not apply and no prepaid loss argument arises. POL-RD-02 governs the remedy, which is arithmetic and not discretionary.

The refund follows from the policy constants. On the booked optimal route: (3.80 base + 0.75 x 18.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 24.0 optimal min) = 24.02, multiplied by the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier = 24.02, plus the 0.80 platform fee, no ERP or tolls on the optimal route, no fixed surcharge, no waiting time fee and no promo discount = a recomputed_fare of 24.8200. Charged_total is 29.68. Refund = 29.68 - 24.82 = 4.86, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and only 16.37% of charged_total, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND and the payable figure rounds UP to SGD 4.90. The fare artifact's own refund block records the same unrounded 4.8600 and payable 4.90.

The zero-refund scenario carried on the fare artifact does not decide anything, because it presupposes the exoneration the trace denies. That closure block reaches a recomputed fare of 29.8750 by setting justified_excess_km to 4.5 - the whole measured excess - and an adjusted optimal of 22.5 km, i.e. by assuming POL-RD-03 applies and excusing the entire deviation. Its intersects_route flag is an input to that scenario, not a finding that limb (c)'s corridor-leaving-and-rejoining test is met, and POL-RD-03 exonerates only where all three limbs hold. Strip out the exoneration and the arithmetic on the booked optimal is the 24.82 / 4.86 / 4.90 figure.

This record should be ruled on, not escalated. The trace's measured geometry and the fare artifact's closure scenario are not mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength under POL-RD-10(7): the geometry check is measured from a 100%-coverage trace at weight 1.0, while the closure block is arithmetic that is conditional on an exoneration the same trace contradicts. No other POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers all match, the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), the timestamps run forward and agree, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact, the computed refund of 4.86 is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total, and every charge line has its counterpart on the record.

There is no pass-through line to add or to net off. The fare breakdown charges no ERP or toll (the erp_lines are empty, total 0.00) and no airport surcharge on a trip that neither originates at an airport nor is billed one, so POL-RD-09 produces no separate ERP correction here - and critically no off-route ERP to be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, which already comprehends only on-optimal-route gantries.

The rider does not overreach, and says so. The 4.5 km / 25% excess sits below the POL-RD-01 materiality line of 8.0 km and 50%, and the driver's profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 399, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established on the only fields POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 permit for that test. The rider therefore claims the POL-RD-02 partial refund of SGD 4.90 and not a refund of the full 29.68 charged, and relies on no rating, account age, lifetime counter or prior-disputes field, all of which POL-GEN-01 makes context only.

ledger.claim: The outcome the rider seeks is a rider win on the record as it stands. The rider filed this dispute, the payment status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, so NO_ACTION would leave the 29.68 charge in place and the rider carrying the disputed amount. PARTIAL_REFUND returns the 4.90 of unjustified distance and time to the rider, which is the only outcome on these numbers that relieves the rider of the disputed charge.

A specific LTA DataMall traffic advisory is on file for this trip: ADV-20260818-055, a HIGH-severity multi-vehicle accident blocking 2 of 3 lanes on the Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit, active 06:09:18 to 07:33:38 on 18 August 2026 — a 59.3 minute overlap with a trip that ran 06:39:18 to 07:08:38 — and the artifact records that the advisory intersects the route. POL-RD-03(a) and POL-RD-03(b) are therefore met on a cited artifact and not on the driver's say-so.

Limb (c) is satisfied on the only geometry the record carries. The trace's own derived advisory-area test records zero fixes inside the advisory's box and a minimum approach of 1203.4 m — which is what an avoiding route looks like, not what a route through the incident looks like: a vehicle that drives the closed segment enters that box, and a vehicle that leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoins after it does not. The driver's contemporaneous in-app message at 06:40:48, 'accident on the PIE ahead, taking the alternative', records him taking the alternative while the advisory was live, not after the fact.

The exoneration is capped, and the cap does not bite on this trip. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is the lesser of the measured 4.5 km and 1.30 x (21.0 - 18.0) + 1.00 = 4.90 km, so the justified excess is 4.5 km — the whole of the measured excess. The closure-adjusted optimal distance is 18.0 + 4.5 = 22.5 km, which is exactly the 22.5 km the trace records, so no unexonerated excess remains to be refunded.

Even on the arithmetic most favourable to the rider — running POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal route rather than the booked one — the recomputed fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 22.5 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 29.8750, against a charged total of 29.68. The refund is floored at zero, and the fare ledger's own derived payable figure is 0.00. There is no sum of money this trip can produce for the rider on the distance and time lines.

The driver has discharged the shifted burden under POL-RD-08 by pointing to a specific artifact and a specific clause — EV-ADVIS-02808-01 and POL-RD-03 — rather than asserting in general terms that traffic was bad. POL-RD-13 does not reach this case: it governs the situation where the bundle holds no traffic_advisory covering the trip window, and here the advisory is present, COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and its window covers the entire trip.

No repeat-deviation uplift and no conduct referral is available against this driver. The excess is 25.0% and 4.5 km, below both the 50% and the 8.0 km limbs, so it is not a MATERIAL deviation and POL-RD-06's profile check is not engaged at all; and on the driver's own trailing-window figures — deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 399 — neither the three-flag test nor the 0.05 ratio test is met, so the FULL_REFUND limb and the POL-RD-06(c) referral both fail.

There is nothing for POL-RD-09 to correct on this fare. The ledger carries no ERP gantry lines at all and tolls_erp is 0.00; the on-optimal-route and off-optimal-route pass-through totals are both 0.00 and the fixed surcharges are 0.0. Where the deviation is exonerated under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-09(2) leaves the distance and time charges standing, and there is no off-route ERP and no phantom gantry line to refund as a standalone correction.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the $29.68 fare stands. The deviation is real, but it is exonerated, and once exonerated the arithmetic returns nothing.

THE DEVIATION IS ESTABLISHED. On the trace figure, which POL-RD-01 makes governing, the trip ran 22.5 km (EV-GPS-02808 trace_distance_km, corroborated by the trip_record copy) against a booked optimal of 18.0 km — an excess of 4.5 km, 25.00% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (above 0.8 km and above 20%). The trace is clean: 177 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, so POL-RD-07 limbs (a)-(c) do not fire, no POL-RD-07(ii) corroboration is needed, and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

POL-RD-03 EXONERATES THE EXCESS. The LTA DataMall advisory ADV-20260818-055 (EV-ADVIS-02808-01, weight 1.0, third-party source) names the Pan Island Expressway towards Tuas after the Eunos Link exit — a segment the optimal route traverses, the artifact recording intersects_route true — and its validity window 06:09:18 to 07:33:38 overlaps the trip (06:39:18 to 07:08:38) by 59.3 minutes. That is limbs (a) and (b), each on a cited artifact. Limb (c) is met on the trace's own geometry: the record's closest available test shows 0 fixes inside the advisory area and a minimum approach of 1,203.4 m, which is what a route that leaves the corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after looks like, and the driver's in-app message at 06:40:48 — sent while the trip was running — records 'accident on the PIE ahead, taking the alternative'.

THE EXONERATION IS CAPPED, AND THE CAP DOES NOT BITE. Justified excess = min(4.5 km measured, 1.30 x (21.0 - 18.0) + 1.00 = 4.90 km) = 4.5 km, so the whole measured excess is justified. The closure-adjusted optimal is 18.0 + 4.5 = 22.5 km, its duration scaled to 30.0 minutes. Running POL-RD-02 against that adjusted route: ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 22.5 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee = 29.875, against a charged_total of 29.68. Refund = 29.68 - 29.875 = -0.195, floored at zero; zero is below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so the outcome is NO_ACTION and the $29.68 is left in place (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0).

Rider, your contrary claims are answered. Limb (c) is not defeated by the trip keeping 1.2 km clear of the incident — staying out of a blocked segment is what avoidance looks like, not evidence against it. Limb (a) is established by the advisory's recorded intersection with the route, not left unproven. Your comparison of the 22.5 km trace with the advisory's 21.0 km shortest lawful alternative does not defeat the cap: POL-RD-03 caps ADDITIONAL distance, and 1.30 x 3.0 + 1.0 = 4.9 km covers the 4.5 km measured. Your $4.90 figure is the correct arithmetic against the booked 18.0 km optimal, but POL-RD-03 requires it to be run against the closure-adjusted 22.5 km optimal, where it returns nothing; the fare artifact's closure block (recomputed_fare 29.875, payable 0.00) is that computation, and it applies.

Your remaining points are accepted and change nothing. There is no rider instruction in the chat log (POL-RD-04, one DRIVER message, waypoint_hint null). No pickup or dropoff amendment, so POL-RD-05 cannot move the baseline (both amendment timestamps and amended_optimal_distance_km are null). Vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12 is out. Fare model is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply. The fare carries no ERP or toll lines (erp_lines empty, total 0.00) and no airport surcharge, so POL-RD-09 has no pass-through correction to add or net off. The deviation is below both POL-RD-01 materiality lines (4.5 km < 8.0 km; 25% < 50%) and the driver's trailing-window figures are deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 399, so no POL-RD-06 uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arise. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so no escalation. No profile field was used as a ground of decision — the reference to rating in the rider's submission was a disclaimer of reliance, and POL-GEN-01 makes it context only.

Confidence 0.85. The ruling rests on EV-ADVIS-02808-01, EV-GPS-02808, EV-TRIP-02808 and EV-CHAT-02808, each at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes, so nothing caps confidence below that and no POL-GEN-02(3) discount narration is required. The monetary effect is nil, so POL-GEN-05 execution is not engaged. This ruling is provisional and either party may appeal it once, within 30 days, under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
